criteria.criterion: `athena --version` (and `-V`) prints the package version, the short source commit from build_info(), and a dirty marker when build_info().dirty is true, e.g. `athena 0.1.0 (abc1234, dirty)`. Check by building with ATHENA_BUILD_COMMIT=abc1234 ATHENA_BUILD_DIRTY=false and running the binary.
criteria.evidence: Not run. The tool hook refused the command: 'Athena policy: environment assignments are not allowed; the environment is set by Athena'. I stopped there and did not look for a way around it. From reading the code: the clap attribute is now `version = wiring::version_string()`. That calls version_text(&build_info()), which formats `{version} ({first 7 chars of commit}{, dirty})`. The unit tests a_clean_build_names_its_short_commit and a_full_hash_is_cut_to_seven_characters pass. The plain-build run under criterion 2 shows that both -V and --version use this string. The code looks correct, but the required run with the build variables set could not be done.
commands: ATHENA_BUILD_COMMIT=abc1234 ATHENA_BUILD_DIRTY=false cargo run -q -p athena-cli --bin athena -- --version; ATHENA_BUILD_COMMIT=abc1234 ATHENA_BUILD_DIRTY=false cargo run -q -p athena-cli --bin athena -- -V

criteria.criterion: A build with no ATHENA_BUILD_COMMIT prints `unknown` as the commit, and is marked dirty (existing build_info() semantics). Check by running a plain `cargo build -p athena-cli` binary.

The text comes from wiring::build_info() (a small formatting function there or in lib.rs, wired into the clap `version` attribute); no build.rs is added, and build_info()'s existing environment handling is unchanged.
criteria.evidence: In the diff, version_string() and version_text() are added to wiring.rs and main.rs uses `version = wiring::version_string()`. The diff leaves build_info() (wiring.rs lines 25-32) untouched. The diff stat lists no build.rs.

criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-cli/tests/binary.rs runs `athena --version` and asserts the output contains the package version and either a hex commit or `unknown`; a unit test covers the formatting for clean, dirty and unknown cases. `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
criteria.evidence: binary.rs adds version_names_the_package_version_and_the_build_commit. It checks both --version and -V for `athena <CARGO_PKG_VERSION> (`, a commit that is `unknown` or hex of 7+ characters, and an optional `dirty`. It passed when I ran it. wiring.rs adds unit tests for the clean, dirty, unknown and full-hash cases, and they passed. Athena's own runs of fmt, clippy and the full cargo test (175 tests) passed.

criteria.criterion: No new non-Rust files; no governance files change.
criteria.evidence: Only four files changed: main.rs, wiring.rs, binary.rs and an existing docs/architecture.md (a one-line table update). No files were added and no governance files changed.

summary: The verdict is fail because I couldn't confirm the first criterion. The block is in how this check runs, not a known fault in the change. That criterion needs a build with `ATHENA_BUILD_COMMIT=abc1234 ATHENA_BUILD_DIRTY=false` set, and the hook refused it ("environment assignments are not allowed"), so I stopped there. Reading the code, the change looks correct. `athena --version` and `-V` now use `wiring::version_string()`, which formats `build_info()` as `<version> (<7-char commit>[, dirty])`. `build_info()` itself is untouched and there is no build.rs. A plain build prints `athena 0.1.0 (unknown, dirty)` for both flags, which I ran. The new unit tests for the clean, dirty, unknown and full-hash cases pass, and so does the new binary test. Athena's fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. Only Rust files and one existing docs table line changed. To finish, someone needs to build with those two variables set and confirm the output is `athena 0.1.0 (abc1234)`.
